details.purpose: To record further details about an individuals death.
details.use: Use to record details about an individuals death.
details.misuse: Not to be used to record cause of death, for specific disease or conditions that caused, or contributed to death, please use the EVALUATION.cause_of_death archetype.

items.items: Details about the death of an individual.
This element is also meant to be usable in a context outside of a death certificate, to state that the individual is deceased without submitting other registrations
Was surgery performed within the last 4 weeks?
Details about why the surgery was performed.
Were the findings used in the certification?
How or in what setting did the patient die?
Please describe how external cause occurred.
If poisoning please specify poisoning agent.
Place of occurrence of the external cause.
Details about pregnancy and infant death.
The definition of viability can be recorded in the Protocol.
If death within 24h specify number of hours survived.

The first weight of the fetus or neonate obtained after birth. For live births, birth weight should preferably be measured within the first hour of life before significant postnatal weight loss has occurred.

While statistical tabulations include 500 g groupings for birth weight, weights should not be recorded in those groupings. The actual weight should be recorded to the degree of accuracy to which it is measured.
What is the age of the mother at the time of death?
Number of completed weeks of pregnancy.
Pregnancy with more than one fetus.
If death was perinatal, please state conditions of mother that affected the fetus and newborn.
Stillbirths and liveborn infants dying within 168 hours [1 week] from birth.
At what stage of labour did the individual die.
Unknown at what time the individual died.
Date of birth of the fetus' or infant's mother.
This number can be deduced if existing data is available in the EHR, but there might also be a need to manually count and record instances
This number can be deduced if existing data is available in the EHR, but there might also be a need to manually count and record instances. The definition of viability can be recorded in the Protocol
Number of pregnancies that do not reach viability from all causes, including spontaneous miscarriages, induced terminations and ectopic pregnancies.
This number can be deduced if existing data is available in the EHR, but there might also be a need to manually count and record instances
Outcome of last previous pregnancy was a live birth.
Outcome of last previous pregnancy was a stillbirh.
Outcome of last previous pregnancy was an abortion.
First (1st) day of last menstrual period.
Child number n in a multiple pregnancy.
When there are multiple individuals in same pregnancy, please state which child in the birth order this registration regards. For example: First twin, second triplet, fifth octuplet
Please specify type of attendant present at birth.
Further specified type of attendant at birth.
For example: witnessed (in or out of hospital)
Approximated or estimated time of death.

Approximated or estimated time of death. For example: based on findings pertaining to examination of the corpse and the pathologist's reconstruction of time of death based on post-mortem changes, temperature, etc.
Specify how or in what setting did the patient die?
Specified place of occurrence of the external cause.
Child number n in a multiple pregnancy.
Specified other multiple. For example: second triplet, fifth octuplet
